propositions: Fourteen test modules hand-build nested pytest invocations with duplicated argv construction, environment handling, and basetemp logic, generating maintenance burden and inconsistency

Three sites lack --basetemp entirely (test_bare_repository_fixture_portability_heldout.py:25, test_git_version_floor.py:164, test_live_jira_xdist_confinement.py:161), creating filesystem isolation defects in nested test runs

A centralized run_nested_pytest(tmp_path, *args, env, timeout=None, cwd=REPO_ROOT, no_cacheprovider=True) helper in tests/_nested_pytest.py must guarantee --basetemp is always present and that caller env is forwarded byte-identically without merge or modification

The helper must preserve all per-site divergences (-n 0, -p no:randomly, --collect-only, per-site timeouts 30/90/300/None) as *args, forward timeout to subprocess.run as a keyword, and return CompletedProcess unmodified so subprocess.TimeoutExpired propagates

An AST-based uniqueness guard must enforce exactly one nested-pytest launch site (the helper) and reject any hand-built [sys.executable, '-m', 'pytest'] list literals across tests/**/*.py except two console-script sites (bug 291e, a371) and marked escapes

Security-critical env contract requires four sites passing minimal dicts with bounded repr to survive verbatim, and PYTEST_DEBUG_TEMPROOT inheritance in two collector/store-isolation children must be preserved by passing env=subprocess_env() rather than None
